thread:
nina: Quick sync: tradeoffs for making preflight both deterministic and fast. I sketched three options: canonical runner (single binary), harness-as-service (internal API), or inline checks in the intake service. Pros/cons?

pat: Inline checks are simplest but couple intake latency to tests. Not great. Canonical runner gives hermeticity but needs distribution. Harness-as-service is flexible but introduces network calls.

ethan: My vote is canonical runner with a thin RPC shim in intake that launches it locally (via container exec). Keeps latency bounded and hermetic.

nina: Concern: cold-start cost for runner if we spin up a container per model. We could keep a warm pool of runners per region.

tracy: Bench-bot: Note that warm pools cost money; propose a hybrid: small warm pool for paid orgs, on-demand for free orgs. Bench scheduling will allocate accordingly.

nina: Also need to settle on artifact schema. Propose flat fields: artifact_id, contract_version, pass_flags (csv), failure_reasons (csv), timestamp, signer. TTL and origin node id. Keep small to fit in model descriptor.

pat: For pass_flags prefer enums rather than free text. Eg PASS_KV,PASS_INT8_PARTIAL,PASS_LONGSEQ. failure_reasons as short codes to keep size down.

ethan: Also think about how models with multi-variant binaries are represented. Suggest descriptor includes variant_id and variant_compat map. Router picks per-variant.

nina: Action: I'll write up canonical runner design + artifact schema. @ethan can prototype exec shim. @tracy to update bench fleet pricing notes.

bench-bot: canonical-runner: repo created (url) template added.

nina: Thanks, keep the sync checks minimal in the intake path. We'll iterate once artifacts land.
